title: Sample Read Count to Functional Categories for Anvi'o Bar Chart
author: Bonnie L Hurwitz
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k3ucynw

steps.title: Access HPC and Prepare Directory
steps.instruction: Log in to the HPC and create a dedicated directory for the functional summary analysis.

substeps.instruction: Login via SSH: ssh hpcocelote ssh hpc ocelote

steps.title: Process Uproc Output into Broad KEGG Categories
steps.instruction: Convert the uproc output files into a summary table of broad KEGG categories for Anvi'o visualization.

substeps.instruction: Use the provided script to convert uproc output (containing gene id, kegg/pfam id, and definitions) into a tab-delimited format.
Map KEGG IDs to broad categories using the reference file /rsgrps/bh_class/kegg_to_broadcat.
Calculate the percentage of reads hitting the top five broad categories for all samples, grouping all remaining categories into 'Other'.
Create a mapping file to convert sample SRR IDs into short sample names.
Generate a final 'samples-table' containing sample name, occlusion, microenvironment, and the counts/percentages for Func1, Func2, Func3, Func4, Func5, and FuncOther.

steps.title: Transfer Data to Local Machine
steps.instruction: Download the generated samples-table from the HPC to your local computer.

steps.title: Initialize Anvi'o Environment
steps.instruction: Launch the Anvi'o Docker container and navigate to the data directory.

substeps.instruction: Move the transferred files to a new folder in Documents (PC users).
If sessions are stuck, use 'docker ps' to find the session ID and 'docker kill [session id]' to terminate it.

steps.title: Create Anvi'o Samples Database
steps.instruction: Generate the samples information database using the processed table.

steps.title: Visualize Results in Anvi'o
steps.instruction: Start the Anvi'o interactive viewer to visualize the sample data.

substeps.instruction: Run command: anvi-interactive -p SAMPLES-MERGED/PROFILE.db -c contigs.db -s samples.db
